analysis: Examined the two CI changes. (1) .github/actions/provider-release-build/action.yml adds a release-lane-only step (head lines 354-367) after the products and cluster-helpers steps. It runs scripts/check-provider-weak-imports.py against the five built binaries (CLI, enclave, fan helper, cluster worker, cluster plan). It uses set -euo pipefail, so a nonzero exit fails the build. Its inputs are step outputs and env vars from earlier trusted steps, quoted in the command. No new secrets, permissions, network access or untrusted-input interpolation. It is purely additive and fail-closed; it reduces the availability risk of shipping binaries that crash on served macOS versions (a DoS-style provider availability concern, adjacent to T-057). The step does not weaken artifact qualification, signing or the cache controls (actions are still SHA-pinned, and cache restore/save are untouched). (2) .github/workflows/ci.yml adds a step (lines 149-155) that runs three local Python scripts: test-check-date-comparisons.py, test-check-provider-weak-imports.py and check-date-comparisons.py. It adds no new triggers, permissions or secrets. Unverified contract: the contents of the three new scripts and scripts/check-provider-weak-imports.py are not supplied, so I could not check their correctness, whether they invoke untrusted binaries unsafely (e.g. via otool/dyld_info), or whether they fail open on unexpected tool output. The step also reads $PROVIDER_SDK_VERSION and $PRODUCT_CLI_NAME from GITHUB_ENV, set by earlier steps. If the checker fails open, the control is just ineffective and no existing control is weakened. No threat-model invalidation identified.
